drivingQuestion: Was the tradition from R' Yoḥanan 'the halakha is like R' Eliezer' — which would presuppose a dispute in this very case — or only 'one inclines' toward him?
outcomeNote: R' Zeira corrects the tradition to מטין rather than הלכה, and Rav Yosef sets the competing versions aside in favour of the ותודיענו formula instituted by Rav and Shmuel.

segments.he: רַבִּי זֵירָא הֲוָה רְכִיב חֲמָרָא, הֲוָה קָא שָׁקֵיל וְאָזֵיל רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין בָּתְרֵיהּ. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וַדַּאי דְּאָמְרִיתוּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין.
segments.en: The Gemara cites the conclusion with regard to this halakha by relating a story: «Rabbi Zeira was riding a donkey» while «Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Avin was coming and walking after him. He said to him: Is» it «true that you said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan» that the «halakha is in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Eliezer» in the case of «a Festival that occurs» directly «after Shabbat?» Since in that case, one cannot recite havdala in the blessing of Who graciously grants knowledge, as it is not included in the Amida prayer on the Festival, there is no alternative but to adopt Rabbi Eliezer’s ruling. «He said to him: Yes.»
The Gemara wonders: Saying that the «halakha» is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer, «indicates that» his peers «dispute» his opinion. Where do we find that dispute?

The Gemara rejects this: «And don’t they dispute» his opinion? «Don’t the Rabbis dispute» his opinion, as, in their opinion the blessing of havdala is recited in the blessing: Who graciously grants knowledge?

segments.he: אֵימַר דִּפְלִיגִי רַבָּנַן בִּשְׁאָר יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה, בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת מִי פְּלִיגִי?
segments.en: The Gemara replies: «Say that the Rabbis dispute» Rabbi Eliezer’s opinion «during the rest of the days of the year,» when the option to recite havdala in the blessing: Who graciously grants knowledge exists, but «in the case of a Festival that occurs» directly «after Shabbat, do they dispute» his opinion? The Rabbis would agree with him in that case.
The Gemara continues: «Doesn’t Rabbi Akiva dispute» his opinion? He holds that havdala is recited as an independent fourth blessing, in which case there is a dispute.

segments.he: אַטּוּ כׇּל הַשָּׁנָה כּוּלָּהּ מִי עָבְדִינַן כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, דְּהַשְׁתָּא נֵיקוּ וְנַעֲבֵיד כְּווֹתֵיהּ?! כׇּל הַשָּׁנָה כּוּלָּהּ מַאי טַעְמָא לָא עָבְדִינַן כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא — דְּתַמְנֵי סְרֵי תַּקּוּן, תְּשַׁסְרֵי לָא תַּקּוּן. הָכָא נָמֵי, שָׁב תַּקּוּן תַּמְנֵי לָא תַּקּוּן.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: «Is that to say that throughout the entire year we act in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Akiva» in this matter, «so that now,» on a Festival that occurs directly after Shabbat, «we will stand and act in accordance with» his opinion? «What is the reason that throughout the whole, entire year, we do not act in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Akiva? Because» the Sages «instituted eighteen» blessings, «they did not institute nineteen» blessings. «Here, too,» the Sages «instituted seven» blessings, «they did not institute eight» blessings. Therefore, Rabbi Akiva’s opinion is not taken into consideration in this case.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָאו ״הֲלָכָה״ אִתְּמַר, אֶלָּא ״מַטִּין״ אִתְּמַר.
segments.en: In response to these questions, Rabbi Zeira «said to him» that «it was not» that «the halakha» is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer «that was stated» in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan, from which one could infer that there was in fact a dispute; rather it was that one is «inclined» to favor the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer «that was stated» in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan.

segments.he: דְּאִתְּמַר, רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבֵּנוּ: הֲלָכָה, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: מַטִּין.
segments.en: «As» indeed «it was stated» that there is a dispute among the Sages in this matter. «Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi said in the name of Rabbeinu,» Rav: «The halakha» is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer. «And some say this» statement: One is «inclined» to favor the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer.

segments.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: מוֹדִים. וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר: נִרְאִין.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yoḥanan said» that there is no dispute here, and the Rabbis «agree» with Rabbi Eliezer. «And Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said» that it was established that Rabbi Eliezer’s opinion «appears» to be correct.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: נְקוֹט דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא בִּידָךְ, דְּדָיֵיק וְגָמַר שְׁמַעְתָּא מִפּוּמָּא דְמָרַהּ שַׁפִּיר כְּרַחֲבָא דְפוּמְבְּדִיתָא.
segments.en: With regard to this difference of opinion «Rabbi Zeira said: Take» this statement of «Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba in your hand, as he is scrupulous and he learned the halakha well from the mouth of its originator, like» the Sage «Raḥava» from the city «Pumbedita.» Raḥava was famous for the precision with which he would transmit material that he learned from his teacher.

segments.he: דְּאָמַר רַחֲבָא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: הַר הַבַּיִת סְטָיו כָּפוּל הָיָה, וְהָיָה סְטָיו לְפָנִים מִסְּטָיו.
segments.en: The Gemara cites an example: «Raḥava said» that «Rabbi Yehuda said: The Temple Mount was a double stav, and there was a stav within a stav.» Here Raḥava used his Rabbi’s language in describing the structure of the Temple and the rows of columns it contained, a row within a row; but he did not employ the common term itzteba, portico, but rather stav, as he heard it from his Rabbi.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אֲנָא לָא הַאי יָדַעְנָא וְלָא הַאי יָדַעְנָא, אֶלָּא מִדְּרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל יָדַעְנָא, דְּתַקִּינוּ לַן מַרְגָּנִיתָא בְּבָבֶל.
segments.en: «Rav Yosef said» the conclusive halakha on this topic: «I don’t know this and I don’t know that, but I do know from» the statements of «Rav and Shmuel they have instituted a pearl for us in Babylonia.» They established a version that combines the first blessing of the Festival with the formula of havdala, parallel to the opinion of the Rabbis who include havdala in the first blessing that follows the first three blessings. They instituted to recite:

segments.he: ״וַתּוֹדִיעֵנוּ ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ אֶת מִשְׁפְּטֵי צִדְקֶךָ וַתְּלַמְּדֵנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת חֻקֵּי רְצוֹנֶךָ, וַתַּנְחִילֵנוּ זְמַנֵּי שָׂשׂוֹן וְחַגֵּי נְדָבָה, וַתּוֹרִישֵׁנוּ קְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת וּכְבוֹד מוֹעֵד וַחֲגִיגַת הָרֶגֶל. בֵּין קְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת לִקְדוּשַּׁת יוֹם טוֹב הִבְדַּלְתָּ, וְאֶת יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה קִדַּשְׁתָּ. הִבְדַּלְתָּ וְקִדַּשְׁתָּ אֶת עַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּקְדוּשָּׁתֶךָ. וַתִּתֶּן לָנוּ וְכוּ׳״.
segments.en: «You have made known to us, Lord our God, Your righteous laws,» «and taught us to perform Your will’s decrees.» «You have given us as our heritage seasons of joy and Festivals of voluntary offerings.» «You have given us as our heritage the holiness of Shabbat, the glory of the festival and the festive offerings of the Pilgrim Festivals.» «You have distinguished between the holiness of Shabbat and the holiness of the Festival,» «and have made the seventh day holy over the six days of work.» «You have distinguished and sanctified Your people Israel with Your holiness,» «And You have given us, etc.»

moves.summary: Sets the scene: R' Zeira riding a donkey with R' Ḥiyya bar Avin walking behind him.
moves.about: the ruling on R' Eliezer for a Festival following Shabbat, which R' Zeira is said to report in R' Yoḥanan's name

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: ודאי דאמריתו משמיה דרבי יוחנן
moves.summary: Asks whether R' Zeira really transmits from R' Yoḥanan that the halakha follows R' Eliezer's mishnaic view on a Festival after Shabbat.
moves.about: whether R' Zeira and his circle really transmit in R' Yoḥanan's name that the halakha follows R' Eliezer when a Festival falls right after Shabbat
confirming that this is indeed what he transmits

moves.summary: Objects that a ruling of 'halakha' presupposes a dispute — where is it?
moves.about: where the dispute is to be found that a ruling 'the halakha is like R' Eliezer' presupposes

moves.summary: Answers that the Rabbis of the mishna do dispute R' Eliezer.
moves.about: there is a dispute — the Rabbis of the mishna dispute R' Eliezer

moves.cueHe: אימר דפליגי רבנן בשאר ימות השנה
moves.summary: Knocks that answer down: the Rabbis dispute only where חונן הדעת is available, not on a Festival.
moves.about: the Rabbis' dispute covers only the rest of the year, not a Festival falling after Shabbat, so it cannot be the dispute presupposed

moves.summary: Presses back: R' Akiva does dispute even here, since he makes havdala a separate blessing.
moves.about: R' Akiva does dispute even in this case, since he makes havdala an independent blessing

moves.cueHe: אטו כל השנה כולה מי עבדינן כרבי עקיבא
moves.summary: Answers that R' Akiva's view is never acted on — a fixed number of blessings was instituted — so his dispute does not count here.
moves.about: the practice does not follow R' Akiva, neither all year nor on a Festival after Shabbat, since a fixed number of blessings was instituted

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: לאו הלכה איתמר, אלא מטין איתמר
moves.summary: Removes the whole difficulty: the word transmitted was מטין, not הלכה.
moves.about: the tradition was not 'the halakha is' like R' Eliezer but 'one inclines', so no dispute need be presupposed

moves.cueHe: דאתמר, רבי יצחק בר אבדימי אמר משום רבנו
moves.summary: Supports the correction from a tradition transmitted in Rav's name in both forms, הלכה and מטין.
moves.about: a second version of the same transmitted ruling, in which the word was מטין and not הלכה

moves.summary: A third term for R' Eliezer's standing: the Rabbis concede to him.
moves.about: in what terms the standing of R' Eliezer's view was transmitted — that the Rabbis concede to him, or that his view appears correct

moves.cueHe: ורבי חייא בר אבא אמר: נראין
moves.summary: A fourth term: his view appears correct.

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי זירא: נקוט דרבי חייא בר אבא בידך
moves.summary: Decides between the versions by the tradent: hold R' Ḥiyya bar Abba's, since he transmits exactly.
moves.about: his version is to be relied on because he is exact and learned the tradition from its master's own mouth, like Raḥava of Pumbedita

moves.summary: Illustrates the standard of exactness with Raḥava, who kept his master's word סטיו.
moves.about: an example of Raḥava's exactness — he kept his master's unusual word סטיו rather than the common term

moves.cueHe: אמר רב יוסף: אנא לא האי ידענא ולא האי ידענא
moves.summary: Declines to choose among the versions and points instead to what Rav and Shmuel instituted in Babylonia.
moves.about: setting the competing versions aside in favour of what he knows from Rav — the formula instituted in Babylonia

moves.cueHe: ותודיענו ה׳ אלהינו את משפטי צדקך
moves.summary: Quotes the ותודיענו formula in full.
moves.about: quoting in full the ותודיענו formula that Rav and Shmuel instituted for a Festival following Shabbat
